description:
FOUND by s531d (s532) while writing the #4361 guard row, NOT fixed (out of the batch).

REPRODUCER (scratch/s531d/p/wait1.pl, worktree agent-a5284a29dfcfe8e48):
  $? = 42; $! = 0; my $r = wait(); print "r=$r status=$? errno=", ($!+0), "\n";
  perl 5.40.3: r=-1 status=-1 errno=10      PCL (10cdc985 and the s531d tree): r=-1 status=42 errno=10

perl's pp_wait stores the result in STATUS whatever it is: with no child, wait() returns -1 AND sets $? = -1 (STATUS_NATIVE_CHILD_SET(-1)).  PCL's wait answers -1 and ECHILD but leaves $? untouched.  Probe waitpid(-1, 0) and waitpid($not_a_child, 0) the same way (perl: $? = -1 for both) before fixing; the fix is one store in the no-child arm of the wait / waitpid runtime functions (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, %p-set-status).


=== DONE (s536h) ===
FIXED (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08, commit 284ab425, cl/ only).  ONE helper %p-wait-status-store (rpid status) for p-wait and p-waitpid, both arms (the no-child host error included): $? = the child's status when a child was reaped (rpid > 0), else -1 -- pp_wait / pp_waitpid's STATUS_NATIVE_CHILD_SET((result > 0) ? argflags : -1).  Probed 5.40.3 and now identical: wait() / waitpid(-1,0) / waitpid(1,0) / waitpid(-1,WNOHANG) with no child -> -1, $? -1, $! ECHILD; waitpid($running, WNOHANG) -> 0 with $? = -1 (PCL stored the poll's UNINITIALISED status word, 551823073); a reaped child's status, a second waitpid of it (-1 / -1), wait() on a child, system and a pipe close unchanged.  Guard Pl/t/system-block-01.t row 47 (FAILS on the base).
subject: wait() / waitpid with no child leaves $? unchanged; perl sets $? = -1 (`$? = 42; wait(); print $?` perl -1, PCL 42)
